subject: Confirming outage window and proposed prorated credit
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@tradewave.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden 503 spike — need confirmed downtime window and credit estimate

Hi Camila,

We observed a sharp spike of 503s affecting our checkout flow between ~02:18–02:55 UTC on Oct 3. This directly impacted ~14% of transactions in that 37-minute period and cost us an estimated $12k in lost orders during a peak promo.

Can Redwood confirm the exact outage window, the root cause if available, and whether TradeWave is eligible for a prorated SLA credit per our contract (SLA section 4.2: 99.95% monthly availability)? We need a formal statement we can share internally and with finance.

I pulled a quick sample of request traces and attached a small log bundle. If you need broader telemetry or traces from the gateway side, let me know what to export.

Thanks,
Samir
VP, Engineering
TradeWave

Attachments: tradewave_request_logs_20271003.zip (log bundle, 4MB)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden 503 spike — need confirmed downtime window and credit estimate

Folks — preliminary findings from the serving plane:
- We see a region-wide transient that caused an elevated rate of 503 responses from the inference tier beginning 02:17:54 UTC and returning to baseline at 02:52:30 UTC.
- Root cause appears to be a shard eviction cascade triggered by a bad autoscaler reaction during a burst of long-sequence requests; kernels GC + shard migration overlapped with a hot key set.
- Affected traffic rate matches TradeWave's token-prefix IDs and the sample traces match our 503 signatures.

Proposed confirmed window for customer-facing statement: 2027-10-03T02:17:54Z — 2027-10-03T02:52:30Z (34m36s).

Per the SLA (monthly uptime target 99.95%), single-region partial outage of this duration maps to a prorated credit calculation. Quick calc: assuming 30-day month (43,200 minutes), 34.6 minutes of downtime -> availability delta = 34.6/43200 = 0.00080 -> availability ~99.919% -> breach of 99.95%.
Estimated credit: pro-rata monthly service fee * 0.00080 (we usually round conservatively).

I’ve attached a short timeline snippet for the customer PDF. Will prepare a sanitized log bundle and an RCAskeleton doc for Marissa to review for EOD.

—Diego
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference

Attachments: timeline_snippet.txt (snippet, 12KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-04T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Draft statement & next steps for TradeWave — please review

Samir — attaching a draft customer-facing statement and a short credit estimate. High level: we confirm an elevated error window and acknowledge a partial availability breach against your contracted SLA.

Key asks:
- Please confirm that the proposed confirmed window (02:17:54Z — 02:52:30Z) aligns with your internal telemetry.
- Confirm whether you want the credit applied as a one-time invoice credit or as a retroactive billing adjustment for Oct.
- If you want an exec-level postmortem review, we can schedule a 30-minute call next week; otherwise we'll send the full RCA doc and recommended mitigations.

I’ve put conservative numbers in the attached doc (postmortem-draft.docx) and listed mitigations: autoscaler tuning, KV cache warmup, and hot-key partitioning.

If I don’t hear back by EOD Tuesday we’ll issue the emailed statement and the credit estimate to finance as a provisional calculation pending your confirmation.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-draft.docx (RCA skeleton, 50KB)
